audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls this a favoured 4/10 lane with a green tone, while the data says Vayne wins 46.59% over 996 games and the level chart (already corrected, and agreeing with the mirror) gives Nasus levels 3 through first item.
audit.why: diff is 'HARD' but diffRating '4/10', report[14] says 'Favoured matchup' and tone is the easy-lane green. Three parts of the same page answer the question differently.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10, hard-lane tone, and the difficulty/summary prose rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] through whys[5] all read as Vayne wins while their rows say Nasus, and spikes[1] sells Final Hour as free dominance at 6.
audit.why: The chart rows were fixed but the explanations were not, so the page renders 'Nasus' beside text saying Vayne shreds him. Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s) gives him bonus health, attack range, armour, magic resist and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown for its duration — that is the level 6 reality.
audit.corrected: whys[2]-[5] and spikes[0]/[1] rewritten around Wither (15s at rank 1), Spirit Fire's armour shred and Fury of the Sands.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is headed 'W-shred his HP (true damage)' but its description is the unrelated 'Nasus wastes Wither' line, and the page never states that Silver Bolts counts abilities.
audit.why: Riot text: Silver Bolts procs on 'the third consecutive attack or ability against the same target' — Condemn advances the stack, which changes every combo count. Confirmed from the mirror audit.
audit.corrected: Silver Bolts counts abilities too — Condemn advances the stack.

audit.whatIsWrong: No text names Siphoning Strike's auto-attack reset as the tell, or its cooldown floor.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is 7.5s at rank 1 falling to 3.5s at rank 5 with an auto-reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Siphoning Strike is 3.5s at rank 5 — deny the cannon and he stalls.

audit.why: Condemn stuns only on terrain collision; in open lane it is a knockback and nothing more. wants.you[2] already says 'A wall behind him for a Condemn stun', which is right.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Wither and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7/10. Wither every 15s and his stacking curve decide it — you win only if his Q count stays low.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Nasus carry threat 10/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Nasus carry threat 10/10.

edits.before: Yours from level 1. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: Yours at level 1 only, then his from 3 through first item. See the chart.

edits.before: Level 3 Silver Bolts true damage shreds his tanky start while you kite Q.
edits.after: At 3 Spirit Fire cuts your armour and Wither halves your kiting speed.

edits.before: Vayne keeps kiting Wither with Tumble and out-damages his stacking.
edits.after: Wither is up every 15s at rank 1 and Tumble cannot outrun it.

edits.after: Silver Bolts shreds his health bar every third attack or ability, but Wither is up every 15s and Spirit Fire strips armour — trade only when Wither is down.

edits.before: Final Hour hands you the invisibility and extra tumble-resets to dodge his Wither and keep stacking your third-hit true damage while he can't touch you.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands adds attack range, resists and %HP damage while Wither pins you from 700 — Final Hour's tumble stealth is your only out, so answer his ult with yours.

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Siphoning Strike is 3.5s at rank 5 — deny the cannon and he stalls.

notes: The packet's own defect list flagged this one: the stored level chart is Vayne 7/7 against a 46.59% win rate. The live page chart has already been corrected to match the mirror (Vayne, Skill, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, Vayne) so I proposed no chart flips — only the ratings and explanations that were still selling a favoured lane. The suspectName hit on whys[4] ('Final Hour's') is a false positive; Final Hour is Vayne's real R name, and that string is being replaced anyway.
